findings.summary: The specification has no effective security requirement for the listed operations. This is a documentation signal; the live API may enforce authentication separately.
findings.impact: If these operations are also unauthenticated at runtime, callers may reach data or actions without signing in.
findings.remediation: Declare the appropriate OpenAPI security requirement and verify authentication is enforced by the API for each operation.

findings.title: An object identifier parameter needs authorization review
findings.summary: An object identifier-like path or query parameter is documented as an integer or string. This is a manual BOLA/IDOR review hint; the schema does not show whether access checks are missing.
findings.impact: If callers can change an identifier and the API lacks object-level authorization, they may access another user's object.
findings.remediation: Verify object-level authorization for every identifier. Consider opaque identifiers where appropriate, while keeping authorization checks as the primary control.

findings.impact: If callers can change an identifier and the API lacks object-level authorization, they may access another user's object.
findings.remediation: Verify object-level authorization for every identifier. Consider opaque identifiers where appropriate, while keeping authorization checks as the primary control.

findings.impact: Large request values or unbounded collection responses can increase memory, CPU, and downstream load when runtime limits are also absent.
findings.remediation: Document realistic maxLength and maxProperties values, enforce request limits in the service, and paginate large collection endpoints.

findings.impact: Large request values or unbounded collection responses can increase memory, CPU, and downstream load when runtime limits are also absent.
findings.remediation: Document realistic maxLength and maxProperties values, enforce request limits in the service, and paginate large collection endpoints.

findings.impact: Large request values or unbounded collection responses can increase memory, CPU, and downstream load when runtime limits are also absent.
findings.remediation: Document realistic maxLength and maxProperties values, enforce request limits in the service, and paginate large collection endpoints.

findings.impact: Large request values or unbounded collection responses can increase memory, CPU, and downstream load when runtime limits are also absent.
findings.remediation: Document realistic maxLength and maxProperties values, enforce request limits in the service, and paginate large collection endpoints.

findings.impact: Large request values or unbounded collection responses can increase memory, CPU, and downstream load when runtime limits are also absent.
findings.remediation: Document realistic maxLength and maxProperties values, enforce request limits in the service, and paginate large collection endpoints.

findings.impact: Large request values or unbounded collection responses can increase memory, CPU, and downstream load when runtime limits are also absent.
findings.remediation: Document realistic maxLength and maxProperties values, enforce request limits in the service, and paginate large collection endpoints.

findings.impact: Large request values or unbounded collection responses can increase memory, CPU, and downstream load when runtime limits are also absent.
findings.remediation: Document realistic maxLength and maxProperties values, enforce request limits in the service, and paginate large collection endpoints.

findings.summary: The specification has no effective security requirement for the listed operations. This is a documentation signal; the live API may enforce authentication separately.
findings.impact: If these operations are also unauthenticated at runtime, callers may reach data or actions without signing in.
findings.remediation: Declare the appropriate OpenAPI security requirement and verify authentication is enforced by the API for each operation.

findings.title: An object identifier parameter needs authorization review
findings.summary: An object identifier-like path or query parameter is documented as an integer or string. This is a manual BOLA/IDOR review hint; the schema does not show whether access checks are missing.
findings.impact: If callers can change an identifier and the API lacks object-level authorization, they may access another user's object.
findings.remediation: Verify object-level authorization for every identifier. Consider opaque identifiers where appropriate, while keeping authorization checks as the primary control.

findings.title: A write request schema may accept mass-assignment fields
findings.summary: A write request permits undeclared object properties or includes a server-managed field without readOnly. These are schema review signals, not proof of how the server binds or authorizes fields.
findings.impact: If the implementation binds untrusted request properties directly to protected model fields, callers may change ownership, role, or other privileged state.
findings.remediation: Use explicit request DTOs or allowlists, reject unexpected properties where practical, and enforce authorization and ownership checks in the server.

findings.title: A response schema contains a potentially sensitive field

findings.remediation: Set a realistic maxItems in the contract and enforce request-size and processing limits in the API.

findings.remediation: Prefer authorization code with PKCE for user authorization or client credentials for machine-to-machine access.

findings.title: An object identifier parameter needs authorization review
findings.summary: An object identifier-like path or query parameter is documented as an integer or string. This is a manual BOLA/IDOR review hint; the schema does not show whether access checks are missing.
findings.impact: If callers can change an identifier and the API lacks object-level authorization, they may access another user's object.
findings.remediation: Verify object-level authorization for every identifier. Consider opaque identifiers where appropriate, while keeping authorization checks as the primary control.

findings.remediation: Use explicit request DTOs or allowlists, reject unexpected properties where practical, and enforce authorization and ownership checks in the server.

findings.remediation: Use explicit request DTOs or allowlists, reject unexpected properties where practical, and enforce authorization and ownership checks in the server.

findings.title: A request or collection response lacks documented resource bounds
findings.summary: Request strings or maps lack schema limits, or a GET response returns a top-level array without a recognizable pagination parameter. These are contract review hints and do not establish runtime resource exposure.
findings.impact: Large request values or unbounded collection responses can increase memory, CPU, and downstream load when runtime limits are also absent.
